shared_context.problem: A construction company is building $5$ identical houses on a ${(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}$ square mile plot of land.

earlier_parts.problem:
Expressed as a single fraction, the exact area of the plot of land is$\,$

                            
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
${\text{mi}}^{2}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The exact area of land is ${(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}\,{\text{mi}}^{2}.$

Writing ${(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}$ with multiplication signs, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2} & ={{\frac{4}{5}\times \frac{4}{5}}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ times}} \\  & =\frac{4\times 4}{5\times 5} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}=\frac{16}{25}.
$$

earlier_parts.problem:
Building company policy states that each ton of cement mixture should contain at least $0.7$ tons of sand. What's the minimum amount of sand in $1.2$ tons of cement mixture? Express your answer as a decimal.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        There will be a minimum of

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
tons of sand in $1.2$ tons of cement mixture.

feedback.worked_solution:
To determine how much sand is in $1.2$ tons of the cement mixture, we have to multiply $1.2$ by $0.7.$

We proceed by multiplying the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers.

Notice that the second number has a leading $0$, which we ignore during the multiplication:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,.7\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,4\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in $1.2$ and there is $1$ decimal place in $0.7.$
Therefore, their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

So, we take our value of $84$ and add a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places.

$$
\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{84}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Hence, $1.2\times 0.7=0.84.$

We conclude that there are $0.84$ tons of sand in $1.2$ tons of the cement mixture.

earlier_parts.problem:
The building company combines $1.6$ tons of sand with $0.69$ tons of cement to make their cement mixture. What is the total weight of the mixture? Express your answer as a decimal.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        The total weight of the mixture is

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
tons.

feedback.worked_solution:
To find the total weight of the mixture, we need to calculate the sum $1.6+0.69.$

There is $1$ decimal place in $1.6$ and $2$ decimal places in $0.69.$

To add the numbers, they both need to have the same number of decimals. Hence, we rewrite the first number so that it has $2$ decimal places:

$$
1.6=1.60
$$

Next, we line up the decimal points:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, &  & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we proceed by adding the two numbers just as we would with whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned} \\ 1\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  &  \\  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, &  & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,.\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total weight of the mixture is $2.29$ tons.

tons of cement mixture are left over.

One of the workers cuts $3\,\frac{3}{4}\,\text{ft}$ from a pipe measuring $5\,\frac{1}{8}\,\text{ft}.$ What is the length of the remaining pipe? Express your answer as a mixed number.

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        The length of the remaining pipe is$\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        
$\text{ft}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
The length of the remaining pipe is $(5\,\frac{1}{8}-3\,\frac{3}{4})\text{ft}.$

Writing $5\,\frac{1}{8}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
5\,\frac{1}{8}=\frac{5\times 8+1}{8}=\frac{41}{8}.
$$

Writing $3\,\frac{3}{4}$ as an improper fraction, we have

$$
3\,\frac{3}{4}=\frac{3\times 4+3}{4}=\frac{15}{4}.
$$

Therefore, our problem now is to work out the following:

$$
\frac{41}{8}-\frac{15}{4}
$$

To subtract two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator.

In this question, we can make a common denominator of $8.$

To put $\frac{15}{4}$ over a denominator of $8,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $2:$

$$
\frac{15}{4}=\frac{15\times 2}{4\times 2}=\frac{30}{8}
$$

We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators:

$$
\frac{41}{8}-\frac{30}{8}=\frac{11}{8}
$$

Finally, we convert back to a mixed number:

$$
\frac{11}{8}=1\,\text{R}\,3=1\,\frac{3}{8}
$$

Therefore, $1\,\frac{3}{8}\,\text{ft}$ of pipe remains.
